title: Header says mark exits 2 for an unknown pass; the code exits 1
detail: The MARK paragraph says 'A pass that is out of order, already done or unknown exits 2 with the file untouched'. Line 170 rejects an unknown --pass with bad() (KitExit 1), and the unit test at test/kit-unslop-ordered-redline-passes.test.js:164 pins exit 1. A probe confirmed it: `mark --state p.json --pass sparkle` exits 1. A caller who branches on the documented exit codes (2 = refusal and retry with the next pass, 1 = broken input) gets the wrong branch. The same text is in .claude/helpers/kit/redline-passes.js:24.
fix_hint: Change the header in both copies to 'A pass that is out of order or already done exits 2; an unknown pass id exits 1'. That matches the code and the test.

title: next/remaining depend on where the first problem sits, so `next` can name a pass already listed as done
detail: evaluate stops at the first problem (line 98) and builds `remaining` only from the ids it saw before that point. For {"done":["spacing","bogus","color"]} it returns next=color and keeps color in `remaining`, although color is in `done`. The header (line 13) says `next` 'still names the first pass of the plan that is not done'. The answer is arguably the right advice, but it contradicts the stated rule. The `fix` text 'Redo the passes out of order' also points at the wrong pass for unknown or repeated ids.
fix_hint: Either reword the header: on a problem, `next` is the first plan pass after the last in-order prefix. Or compute `next` from the in-order prefix explicitly and word `fix` for each problem kind.

title: Concurrent-mark test does not check why the losers failed
detail: 'serialises concurrent marks' asserts only that at least one mark succeeded and that the file holds an in-order prefix. A loser that failed with a lock timeout or a lost-lock KitExit 1 would also pass the test, although the behaviour the spec needs is a refusal (exit 2).
fix_hint: Also assert that every rejected result is a KitExit with code 2, and that done.length equals the number of fulfilled results.

title: next signature line omits batch, reminder and exit
detail: The return shape documented for `next` is { next, done, remaining, ok, problem?, fix? }. The code can also add `batch` and `reminder` (--all-at-once) and `exit: 2` (--strict). The ALL AT ONCE and STATE paragraphs describe these, but the signature line, which readers scan first, does not.
fix_hint: Extend the line to { next, done, remaining, ok, problem?, fix?, batch?, reminder?, exit? } in both copies.

title: from-brief on real assume output prefills product from assumed placeholders and marks it done
detail: The header says from-brief accepts design-brief's assume output ({ kind, brief }). Real assume output always fills every field, using the kind's default text for any answer that is missing, and lists those defaults in `assumptions`. fromBrief ignores `assumptions`, so offer and audience always look answered. Probe: `echo '{"kind":"ui","answers":{}}' | cli.js design-brief assume | cli.js direction from-brief` returns product.text "one clear job for the screen, taken from the request, for a regular user on desktop and phone, so the layout is responsive and moderately dense." with todo: false and prefilled: ["product"]. The same happens when only the offer was given: the audience becomes the default string. So the skeleton presents generic filler as the user's product line and tells them it needs no answer, which defeats the verb's purpose on a documented input. The unit test 'accepts the assume output shape' uses a made-up { kind, brief: { offer } } that real assume never produces, which is why the bug was missed.
fix_hint: When the input has `brief`, treat each field named in `assumptions[].field` as missing (do not prefill offer or audience from it, set todo: true and add a note). Add a test that pipes real `assume()` output (from design-brief.js) through fromBrief, with no answers and with offer only.

title: JSON moments array is re-split on 'and' and commas, so two moments count as three
detail: fromJson joins a moments array with '; ' and judge() then counts items() on the joined string. items() also splits on ',', 'and', '&' and '+', so a moment written as an array element is split again. Probe: moments ["the total and subtotal row", "the print button"] gives too_many_moments (counted as 3) even though the user gave exactly two places. The array form is the one input where the count is known for certain, yet it gets the heuristic's false positives, and with --strict it exits 2.
fix_hint: Keep the array length from fromJson (for example store values.__count.moments = v.length) and use it for the too_many_moments check instead of items(); add a test with an array element that contains 'and'.

title: On an out-of-order state, remaining and --all-at-once batch silently drop the misplaced pass
detail: evaluate() adds the offending id to `seen` before the loop stops, and `remaining` is IDS minus `seen`. For done=["spacing","motion"] (probed via cli.js) `next --all-at-once` returns ok=false and remaining/batch = color..visuals, with no motion. The fix text tells the user to redo the passes in plan order, but the list it hands back as 'the whole remaining list' leaves out a pass that still has to be applied in order. An agent that follows the batch never does motion. The same happens with plain `next`: `remaining` names 7 passes instead of 8. No test covers remaining or batch on a broken state.
fix_hint: Build `remaining` from the in-order prefix only (IDS.slice(prefixLength)), or skip seen.add for the offending id when the problem is 'order'. Add a test that done=["spacing","motion"] gives remaining/batch = IDS.slice(1).

title: parseFlags looks flags up on a plain object, so Object.prototype names are accepted as flags
detail: `spec[a]` finds inherited members: `next toString x`, `next constructor x` or `mark ... valueOf y` find a truthy function, take the next argument as its value and exit 0 instead of the documented exit 1 'unexpected argument' (`next toString x` probed: exit 0).
fix_hint: Use Object.hasOwn(spec, a) (or a Map / Object.create(null) spec) before reading kind.

title: Header says every bad `done` is reported by next as ok=false, but non-string ids exit 1
detail: STATE says '`done` must be an array of pass ids ...; anything else is reported by `next` as ok=false with a `problem` (an unknown id, ...)'. readState throws exit 1 for {"done":[1]} before evaluate runs (the test 'nums.json' expects that), so a non-string entry is not an ok=false advisory answer. The unknown-id branch in evaluate for non-strings cannot be reached through run.
fix_hint: Say in the header that a non-string entry (like a missing `done`) exits 1, or drop the readState check and let evaluate report it as unknown.

title: A refused mark still creates the state file's folder
detail: withStateLock creates the parent folder before the order check runs, so `mark --state sub/x.json --pass color` exits 2 ('file untouched') and leaves an empty `sub/` directory behind (probed). Small, but it contradicts 'refusal leaves things untouched' for a new path.
fix_hint: Check the order against a lock-free read first and refuse before taking the lock, then re-check inside the lock; or document that the folder is created.

title: JSON array of blank strings passes as a present field instead of missing
detail: fromJson joins array elements with '; ' before checkFields trims, so {"moments": [" ", ""]} becomes text ';' (present: true, no problems) and ["","",""," "] becomes '; ; ;' with count 0. The missing check never fires, so with the other four fields valid, check returns ok: true and --strict exits 0 for an empty moments line (probed via cli.js direction check). The same applies to any field given as an array. The .claude/helpers copy has the same code. No test covers it.
fix_hint: Drop blank elements before joining (v.map(x => x.trim()).filter(Boolean).join('; ')) so an all-blank array gives '' and reports missing; add a test for moments: [' ', ''].

title: Arrays are accepted for every field, but the docs and error message say only moments
detail: The array branch has no id === 'moments' guard, so {"character": ["patient"]} is accepted and joined, yet the header says 'moments may be an array of strings' and line 179's error offers the array form only for moments. A wrong-shaped input for other fields is accepted without an error.
fix_hint: Limit the array branch to id === 'moments', or document that every field accepts an array of strings.

title: Exact duplicate JSON keys: last one wins silently, while text input says first wins and flags it
detail: JSON.parse keeps the last of {"product":"a","product":"b"} (probed: text 'b', no problem), and the 'given more than once' guard at line 174 only catches case variants. The markdown path reports duplicate_field and keeps the first. So the same mistake behaves differently depending on the input format.
fix_hint: Document that duplicate JSON keys are last-wins, or detect exact repeats (for example with a reviver or a light key scan) and report duplicate_field.

title: Non-object JSON (null, an array) on check is read as markdown and reported as five missing fields
detail: Only a leading '{' routes to fromJson, so a JSON file containing null or ["Product: a"] goes to parseText and returns ok:false with five 'missing' problems and exit 0. The 'direction JSON must be an object' error in fromJson can never be reached from the CLI. This follows the documented sniffing rule, but the user gets a misleading message instead of a clear input error.
fix_hint: Also treat a leading '[' (or text that parses as JSON) as JSON, so fromJson's object error is shown with exit 1.

title: JSX input: code after the first tag is scanned as visible copy
detail:
visibleText (jsx) blanks only the text before the first TAG_RE match. After that, seg() blanks only brace groups that open and close inside one tag-to-tag segment and nest at most two levels deep. A function body broken up by JSX tags, top-level statements, or a TS generic (useState, forwardRef, Array, all matched as tags) therefore reaches the copy detectors as raw code. Probe: a plain two-component .jsx file (Header returns

Projects

; Footer has `const port = 1234;` and `throw new Error('year is required!')`) gives fake-data on line 6 and exclamation-marks on line 7, and `scan --strict --file b.jsx` exits 2. A shadcn-style forwardRef Button gives the same false hits. The header promises that copy signs read visible text only, and the workflows block on --strict, so ordinary component files fail the gate because of their code.
fix_hint: For jsx, take visible text only from JSX children: the text between a tag's '>' and the next '<' or '{' while inside an element, with a depth count of open and close tags. Blank everything outside elements and every {...} expression. Do not treat a '<Ident...>' that follows an identifier or '(' as a tag. Add a regression test with two components, a TS generic and an Error('...!') string, and assert zero copy hits.

title: Markdown fence closing ignores fence length and info string
detail:
maskCode closes a fence on any line that starts with three or more of the same fence character. CommonMark requires the closing fence to be at least as long as the opener and to carry no info string. So a ````md block that shows a ```js example ends at the inner ```, and a line '```js' inside a block is taken as a close. Code after that point is then scanned as prose. Probe: '# T

```js
const a = "x!";
```js
Welcome back!
```' on stdin reports greeting-headline and exclamation-marks on line 6, which is inside the code block. Docs that show markdown or code samples are a normal input for this verb.
fix_hint: Record the opener's character and length. Close only on a line matching ^ {0,3}(char){len,}[ \t]*$. Add a nested-fence test.

title: A README that opens with an HTML block is sniffed as html, so its fenced code is scanned
detail:
sniff returns md only when the text does not start with '<' (`!/^<[a-z]/i.test(t)`). Many READMEs open with a centred logo block such as

and then use # headings. Those are sniffed as html, and --file ignores the .md extension by design, so the markdown masking (fences, inline code) never runs. Probe: such a README.md with a ```sh fence containing echo "done!" and inline `x!` gives format html and exclamation-marks hits on lines 8 and 11, both of which are code. Without --format md the user gets wrong hits, and --strict blocks on them.
fix_hint:
Let a leading run of HTML block lines fall through to the markdown check. For example, test the md signals on the text with leading HTML blocks stripped, or count a line-start '# ' heading or fence anywhere in the text as md even when the text opens with a tag. Add a test for a README that starts with a logo

.
